newsitem.title: CHINA: Deng kin oppose China's top conservative ideologue.
newsitem.headline: Deng kin oppose China's top conservative ideologue.

text.p: China's top conservative ideologue Deng Liqun has been left off the high-profile funeral committee for paramount leader Deng Xiaoping at the request of the dead man's family, Chinese sources said on Sunday.
"Deng Xiaoping's children did not want Deng Liqun on the funeral committee," said one source with close ties to the ruling Communist Party.

The family was opposed to Deng Liqun sitting on the funeral committee because he had been openly critical of Deng Xiaoping after the patriarch's 1992 tour of southern China that kick-started the faltering economy, the source said.
"It was a slap in the face to Little Deng," another source said.
Deng Liqun, who is not related China's late paramount leader, was China's propaganda chief for several years under Deng and had been personally loyal to him for years.
He served often as Deng's speechwriter and Deng several times unleashed the ideological hardliner to check more liberal party leaders.

The 459-member funeral committee was a virtual "who's who" of China's Communist leaders, an important indication of who's in and who's out in the arcane world in the highest echelons of the secretive ruling party.
Deng Xiaoping died in Beijing on Wednesday aged 92. China will cremate Deng on Monday and hold a memorial service on Tuesday in the cavernous Great Hall of the People in Beijing.
